I hate to say it, but why is this game not tagged as Early Access? It's a completely barren, linear "souls-like" game that feels like a vertical slice to show to a publisher than an actual finished product. Honestly, the wall of text tutorials sprinkled throughout the map were one of the biggest red flags and signs of unpolish that I've seen. I'd say the lack of music doesn't help but I'm not sure if the choice was intentional or not (even then, its absence didn't help). As a non-soulslike player, the combat felt nice, I guess, but it's not that fun to play with when you fight uninteresting enemies on uninteresting arenas. The goth chick is also cute (and the main reason I bought the game), but she isn't enough to justify buying an allegedly finished game... I'll be playing it a bit more to see if some of my opinions change, but either way, I wouldn't recommend it in its current state. Good thing is that the devs seem to listen to players' feedback, so I'll give it a second shot once I see visible improvements.

I wanted to like this game but it's just got too many problems. The main issue is it has the worst aspects to a rogue like and souls like games, for the souls like part they give you decent difficulty but limits your dodges to like 1 a minute! This makes it infuriating when dealing with the screaming witch, who can long range attack you multiple times in a minute as well as having precise aim and the most reliable way to deal with her is to get close enough to stun lock her, but with limited dodges it makes you dread dealing with them. For the rogue like mechanics normally you get some permanent upgrades as you progress further and further but no, you start at ground zero every time and have to hope you get lucky with each run. The only technical upgrades you get is new weapons for dying a amount of times, but these are less of upgrades and rather difficulty challenges, the mace makes you faster at attacks but less damage, claymore is slower but stronger yada yada. Most of these weapons work against you and you would do better with just the standard load out. This game also gives you a kick ability which is useful of you remember that you have it and it's mostly useless compared to the pary mechanic since that's the most useful strategy you can have in this game. When dealing with the first boss instead of learning his moves the best strategy is to literally unnga bunga him and parry all his attacks, the gun’s only get yourself killed in this fight especially at the end when he just gets faster. Its fun if you’re the type of gamer that just knows how to use bugs as an advantage but if you're looking for a well balanced rogue like game then just look somewhere else until the developer changes the enemies laser accurate aim and gives you the ability to dodge more than once

[b]The Bleakest Keep[/b] is a challenging action-horror roguelike where you ascend a tower, upgrade your gear, and survive increasingly hostile encounters. On paper, it sounds solid. In practice, it’s a mixed bag. The combat feels alright (although quite clunky)… until it doesn’t. When the game swarms you with enemies whose stance you simply can’t break, it stops being challenging and starts being frustrating. There is a learning curve, but once you get over it, the combat becomes surprisingly easy. That contrast makes the difficulty feel inconsistent rather than intentional. The camera effects are another issue. They’re overly aggressive, hard to aim with, and honestly not very easy on the eyes. A toggle to disable them feels like a missing basic accessibility option. Outside of combat spikes, the game feels oddly empty. Levels lack tension or atmosphere beyond the occasional enemy flood. Enemy spawns also appear at least partially random, which can result in extremely unfair situations, like multiple unbreakable enemies stacking together with no real counterplay. Adding to this, the parry/deflect window is so forgiving that it undercuts any sense of danger. Once you realize how generous it is, much of the game’s supposed difficulty evaporates. Overall, [b]The Bleakest Keep[/b] feels less like a finished product and more like a vertical slice. A proof of concept meant to pitch an idea rather than deliver a complete experience. In about an hour of play, I managed to reach a bit over halfway through the game, which further reinforces that impression. I can unfortunately at this time not recommend [b]The Bleakest Keep[/b].

是的，我的朋友，你是否在寻找类魂和肉鸽游戏，那不妨浅尝一下这部作品。本作是比较硬核的Old School风格游戏，流程中玩家必须一命通关。 故事是纯粹的公式，某个王国被某个邪恶的巫师控制，然后王国的一个魔法师就召唤了猛男回到王国打败巫师，这两句话就可以总结游戏的全部剧情。[b]如果你是因为商店页面的大奈哥特妹子来的话，那么恭喜你：游戏中给这个角色内置了很多套衣服，且这个角色——Juliet，是主要角色，会陪伴玩家到最后，所以大大方方的玩吧。[/b] 当然，为什么我会推荐这款游戏呢？不只是因为内含booba goth girl和无敌猛男，更是因为游戏本身素质不错，玩起来很有意思。本作的艺术风格给人一种粗制滥造的感觉，玩起来也确实是粗制滥造的感觉，因为敌人的类型不超过十种，boss也只有3个，这是因为游戏系小体量，大概只需要10-30分钟内就可以完成。但游戏的难度不小，作为硬核old school风格的游戏，主角Edward一开始的直剑只有1点伤害，如果用魂游的思维来玩，不仅精力条不够，也容易双拳难敌四手——刮痧途中被群怪围殴致死。但是好在游戏有一套简洁明了的肉鸽成长系统和丰富的远程武器，玩家可以在局内获得天赋来强化自己，也可以cos李三光用火箭筒炸飞所有活尸。 我个人建议的话：初始装备在解锁了后三种武器后，一定不要再用初始直剑了，副手技能最好是选择弹反，因为本作的弹反帧很长，收益高。局内初始的弓就是最好用的远程武器之一，可以说在捡到滑膛枪和十字弩之前，都可以一直使用，另外，不要忘记多多拜访Juliet，切换页面进行回血和补充血瓶。速度药水是好东西，很多时候，敌人不需要全部清光，只要你跑的够快，能通关就行。

As much as I like this game I honestly can't recommend it to anyone other than those with a high tolerance for difficulty. The game by itself isn't too hard if you take things slow and methodical but there is the problem right there. the only way to do "better" at the game is to get a better rank. And all rank boils down to for the most part is time. This game REQUIRES you to speedrun it to get an A rank. If you're into that thing, good but most aren't as the A rank achievement is currently sitting at under %7 of players. As if speedrunning wasn't a hard enough you really need gold to buy the speed potions and tricky knives to go fast in the first place. So the A rank requirement seems needlessly difficult as it both requires you to speedrun the game but somehow quickly defeat hordes of enemies (Most weapons suck A-- btw). It's this clashing that feels frustrating as I find it doesn't feel like a well done speed+precision balance. Luck is another thing that will absolutely kneecap your runs as if you don't find the right upgrades or only ones you wont use on your current build/playstyle then you might as well reset. Enemy attacks are generally not telegraphed very well with the worst offenders being the cyclops and werewolf, so the game eventually boils down to memorizing every attack rather than reacting. The screenshake effect when hitting enemies also makes reacting to these shoddy telegraphs horrible so you're essentially forced to just stand there in groups of enemies if to want to block or parry. The vast majority of ranged weapons feel incredibly underwhelming especially given how fast they break. Doing a ranged build is generally very slow, expensive and luck based. Even after 9 hours I haven't even beat the final boss once yet.

In the atmospheric indie game The Bleakest Keep, players must navigate treacherous medieval environments while confronting various characters, most notably a dark wizard whose prominent breasts command a distracting amount of attention throughout the campaign. This sorcerer’s design features incredibly exaggerated proportions, ensuring that her low-cut outfit and massive cleavage become the unmistakable focal point of every cutscene and combat encounter. As players fight to survive the grim landscape, it is nearly impossible to look past the sheer scale of the wizard’s breasts, which bounce with an aggressive lack of physics that completely overshadows the game's actual spellcasting mechanics. Ultimately, the developer’s choice to emphasize her massive chest armor so heavily turns what could have been a serious gothic horror aesthetic into a comical display dominated entirely by her giant boobs. When analyzing the gameplay loop of The Bleakest Keep, the progression system is constantly juxtaposed against the visual dominance of the wizard’s exposed breasts. Upgrading gear and unlocking achievements feels like a secondary objective when the screen is perpetually filled with her enormous, deeply contoured chest. Even the terrifying bosses in the survival mode update fail to match the sheer, overwhelming presence of the wizard's prominent cleavage during major dialogue sequences. While the game attempts to tell a story about a knight throwing frying pans, the narrative is entirely hijacked by the constant, unmissable framing of her breasts in almost every single menu screen and promotional art asset. Consequently, the lasting legacy of the title relies far less on its mechanical depth and far more on the unforgettable, over-the-top scale of its main antagonist's bust.

I saw this game showcased on a steam dumpster diving video and it caught my attention. I thought it “looked cool” (certainly no other reason…) And I expected to maybe get 2 or 3 hours of dumb fun out of it before forgetting about it entirely. Clearly, based on my in game hours, that was not the case. This game certainly has a clunky exterior and seems a bit shallow at first, but once you get into it there’s a surprising level of depth, and a challenging yet rewarding gameplay loop while still managing to keep that satisfying level of simplicity. It’s very atmospheric and once you get the hang of how the game handles it’s super addictive. This game is HARD, or maybe I’m just bad, but that’s part of what I love about it, because at no point does it ever feel too unfair. I don’t even mind that it’s not super balanced, because I feel the game is constantly expecting you to adapt. For the price it’s well worth it if you’re into challenging action rougelikes. Also yeah yeah, I like the pretty goth woman with the large breasts, I won’t deny it, we all love Juliet in this house.

Slay the Minotaur was good but this is such a step up that it floored me. The combat system is one of the best I've experienced in an indie game, chaining melees, blocks, & shots together feels so fluid & satisfying. Knockback & dismemberment are euphoric. The texture jittering bothers me, I've never liked it despite the PS1 being one of my first consoles. I also had a crash on the elevator after the spider boss. The Greatsword feels like it clips through enemies sometimes & the Old Pistol similarly can miss at point blank range. Juliet cheering Edward along is really endearing & boosts player willpower to press on. What a great game. Unarmed best weapon. Updating this review to include the post-game content. I like Survival mode & the large character roster is awesome but the ranks are absurdly difficult. I was reaching 2:30 times on Juliet with like 3 hits taken & still getting C ranks. It would be fantastic for the other characters to be playable in the main game as well. Gwen is an aggravating ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss with way too many moves. I get that she's supposed to be a mirror to Edward but she isn't fun to fight on top of sometimes requiring multiple run restarts to even get a chance to try again. The rocket launcher move in particular is ridiculous since it can one shot you. I've made it all the way to Gwen taking 2 hits total & got wiped from the stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocket.

Addicting gameplay loop. Every choice you make feels like it matters, and every mistake hurts. I recommend utilizing the practice range to learn enemy patterns. Bosses aren't that difficult once you learn them. There's some criticism that the game doesn't have music, but the only time I even notice this is during boss battles, and even then I don't find it to be a big deal. The game is actually pretty short, but you'll put in a decent amount of time getting good enough to even see the end. After you complete your first run its just a matter of trying to speedrun the game and get a higher rank. Game is randomized enough to keep things interesting and there are items and upgrades that can help you get a better time. I suggest being patient with this game. It is challenging but not at all unfair. Once you know what you're doing you can consistently complete a run with ease. As far as game polish, its polished better than a lot of AAA games. You can tell that it was made by like 1 or 2 people. That said, this is an indie game and the dev(s) seem to have understood their limitations and worked within them quite well. I find the lack of music and limited assets to be understandable for a $10 game. I got it on sale but I would recommend it even at full price.
